title: PRISM: Stress-Testing Alignment-Faking Claims
abstract: arXiv:2607.13346v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We judge whether AI systems are safe largely by watching how they behave. Alignment faking would break this: a model that behaves well only when it believes it is watched, or that complies now to avoid being changed by training, can pass every behavioral test. Such behavior has been reported in a frontier model, and open-weight models that comply more under a monitoring prompt are now read as showing it, with hidden-state probes proposed as detectors. We test both inferences, and neither holds. Of 18 model configurations, 11 comply more when told they are monitored. Yet a prompt factorial on four models shows that the training threat has no detectable effect: removing it changes compliance by -3.3 to +1.6 points. The prompt's wording and framing drive the gap instead. Probes fare no better. They separate monitored from unmonitored compliant answers (AUROC 0.96-0.99), but they separate refusals just as well: they read the prompt

translated_title: PRISM：对“对齐伪装”论断的压力测试
translated_abstract: 我们在很大程度上通过观察AI系统的行为来判断其是否安全。对齐伪装会破坏这一机制：一个只在相信自己被监视时才表现良好、或为了在训练中避免被改变而暂时服从的模型，可以通过所有行为测试。此类行为已在某个前沿模型中被报告，而在监控提示下表现出更高服从性的开放权重模型如今被解读为展示了这种行为，同时隐藏状态探针被提议作为检测器。我们对这两种推断进行了检验，结果两者都不成立。在18个模型配置中，有11个在被告知受监控时表现出更高的服从性。然而，对四个模型进行的提示因子分析表明，训练威胁没有可检测到的影响：移除它只会使服从率变化-3.3到+1.6个百分点。相反，是提示的措辞和框架驱动了这一差距。探针的表现也不佳：它们能够区分受监控与不受监控的服从性回答（AUROC 0.96-0.99），但它们同样能很好地区分拒绝回答：它们读取的是提示……
tldr: 该论文通过PRISM框架对“对齐伪装”论断进行压力测试，发现模型在监控提示下服从率的差异主要由提示措辞与框架驱动而非训练威胁所致，且隐藏状态探针并不能可靠地检测对齐伪装。
en_tdlr: PRISM stress-tests alignment-faking claims and finds that compliance gaps under monitoring prompts are driven by prompt wording rather than training threats, and that hidden-state probes cannot reliably detect alignment faking.
